transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

This is usually caused by water/cleaner residue around the ignition electrodes or under the control knobs after cleaning. The hob keeps trying to spark until it dries out.

Do this now:
1. Turn all burner knobs fully off.
2. If it plugs in, switch it off at the wall / unplug it. If it is hard-wired, turn off the hob circuit at the consumer unit if you can safely identify it.
3. Remove the pan supports and burner caps/rings. Dry everything thoroughly with kitchen roll, especially the small white ceramic spark plugs beside each burner.
4. Leave the hob to dry for at least several hours — ideally 24 hours. A fan in the room can help. Don’t use a hairdryer on high heat or spray more cleaner/water into it.
5. Check that burner caps are refitted correctly and sitting flat before turning it back on.

Also wipe around the knobs: liquid can get behind them and make a switch think it is being pressed. Don’t force or dismantle gas controls.

Important:
• If you can smell gas, hear hissing, or a burner is trying to light when gas is on: turn off the gas supply if safe, ventilate the room, don’t use electrical switches/flames, and contact your gas emergency service.
• If it is still clicking after being properly dry for 24–48 hours, keep the electrical ignition switched off and arrange a qualified gas appliance engineer (for example, Gas Safe registered in the UK). A faulty ignition switch or electrode may need replacing.

It’s annoying, but after cleaning it is very often just trapped moisture.

ok i unplugged the hob (plug is in the cupboard under the sink) and left it all afternoon and its stopped clicking. no gas smell. one cap was a bit wonky so i put it back right. is it ok to plug it back in now?

Yes — if everything is dry, all knobs are fully off, and the burner caps are correctly seated, it’s reasonable to plug it back in.

Do it with dry hands, then:

1. Plug it in and listen for a minute or two with all controls off.
• No clicking: good sign.
• Clicking starts again: unplug it and leave it to dry longer, ideally overnight/24 hours.

2. If it stays quiet, test each burner one at a time briefly. Make sure it lights normally, then turn it fully off.

3. Don’t leave it unattended for the first little while after reconnecting.

A wonky burner cap can definitely cause ignition problems, so reseating it may have fixed it. If the clicking comes back despite everything being dry and correctly fitted, leave it unplugged and get a qualified gas appliance engineer to check the ignition system.
